subject: Pricing sandwich, uplift corridor and channel margin for AWS private offer
messages:
From: Andrew Moore <andrew.moore@cloudworks.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cloudworks.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing sandwich, uplift corridor and channel margin question

Hi Naomi / Sarah —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving to shape a private offer on AWS and I want to make sure we align on two things before we hand this off to Procurement:

1) Channel margin mechanics: CloudWorks will route through two resellers in different regions. We need to understand how Redwood prefers to treat the reseller uplift (is it a true pass-through credit, billed to us, or a net-retention carve?).

2) "Pricing sandwich" (our internal term): we want a short-term anchor discount for go-live, a mid-term committed blended price, and a small renewal uplift corridor. What's your tolerance on anchor discount caps and how that interacts with reserved-commit tiers?

High-level asks from our side so Procurement can build the PO: estimated 12-month commit by SKU (I can share a rough file), desired net effective price target, and whether you can provide an example term sheet showing channel uplift math.

Can you point us to an example structure or send a simple breakout (list, discount, reseller uplift, passback mechanics) so we can validate internally?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

Andrew
Andrew Moore
Head of Cloud Economics, CloudWorks
+1 415-555-0191
[Attachment: purchase_requirements_template.xlsx (stub)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Moore <andrew.moore@cloudworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sandwich, uplift corridor and channel margin question

Andrew — thanks for the clear framing. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Irene (pricing & partner ops) so we can give you the concrete math. Quick answers up front:

- Reseller uplift: we support both pass-through crediting and net-retention models. For AWS private offers we commonly do a pass-through credit to the customer invoice (customer sees a credit line), or alternatively we anchor to a slightly higher list price and allocate a reseller commission from the margin. Each approach has accounting and marketplace listing implications; we can show both.

- Anchor discount caps: we typically cap initial anchor discounts so subsequent committed pricing doesn’t overly erode partners' economics. Typical cap range we work with is 20–35% off list depending on commit band and whether the uplift is handled as a separate credit.

What we need from you to produce the term sheet and channel math:
- rough 12‑month SKU mix (units / usage bands) — the template you attached works great
- target net effective price per SKU or blended target (this lets us back into list discounts + uplift)
- preferred channel model: pass-through credit vs. gross-up reseller commission

I'll ask Ben to prepare a short term-sheet prototype and Irene will outline the channel passback flow (invoice-level versus marketplace credit).

Internal link: https://drive.redwood/company/pricing-playbook-v2.pdf — I'll highlight the pass-through examples.

If you're free Thurs 6/10 at 10am PT we can walk the numbers live.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[phone]

From: Andrew Moore <andrew.moore@cloudworks.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cloudworks.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sandwich, uplift corridor and channel margin question

Naomi — thanks, that helps. Quick clarification items from Procurement: 

- CloudWorks favors a pass-through credit applied at invoice time to simplify our recon. That said, our resellers need a predictable commission to fund onboarding. Can you model both: 1) pass-through credit to CloudWorks with resellers invoiced directly, and 2) grossed-up reseller commission baked into the private offer so resellers get funded via the marketplace flow?

- Commit: provisional SKU mix attached (small/med/large runtime instances + embeddings units). We're targeting a blended net effective of roughly $0.0024/token equivalent across the 12m commit, with ~10% growth in Q4.

- Can you include an example invoice-level credit line so our accounting team can validate treatment?

I'll confirm availability for Thurs 6/10 10am PT.

Thanks — attaching the fillable template you asked for.

Andrew
[Attachment: cloudworks_sku_mix_provisional.csv (stub)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Moore <andrew.moore@cloudworks.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: CloudWorks private-offer term sheet + channel margin breakout

Andrew — attaching a draft term sheet and a simple SKU x channel breakout. Please review; this is a conservative starting point intended to keep reseller economics intact while meeting your blended target. Highlights below: 

- Offer model A (pass-through credit): list price unchanged, private-offer discount 30% applied to CloudWorks invoice; reseller commission paid separately as a % of net list and issued as a marketplace-managed credit to reseller account. Invoice-line example included.

- Offer model B (grossed-up): private-offer uses a higher list price but standard discount of 25% to CloudWorks; reseller commission of 8% is embedded in the list/gross-up so resellers are funded from the transaction.

- Anchor discount cap: 35% max for the initial 90-day go-live, stepping to the committed discount after usage validates the baseline. Renewal uplift corridor: 3–7% depending on commit attainment.

Sample channel margin table (excerpt):
- SKU: runtime.large | List: $0.12/token | Offer A discount: 30% | Effective to CW: $0.084 | Reseller uplift (pass-through): 9% of list ($0.0108)
- SKU: embed.16k | List: $0.00075/embedding-unit | Offer B discount: 25% | Effective to CW: $0.0005625 | Reseller commission (embedded): 8% of list ($0.00006)

Attachments: cloudworks_private_offer_term_sheet.pdf (term/legal boilerplate), sku_channel_margin_breakout.xlsx (detailed math). Also included a short invoice mock that shows the pass-through credit line.

DocuSign: if this looks good we can send a term sheet via DocuSign (https://docusign.com/link/sample-cw-term) to speed approvals.

Next steps I propose:
- You review the attached sheet and return comments by EOD Fri 6/11
- If you prefer model A vs B, call that out and we’ll finalize the mechanics for marketplace listing and reseller payments

—Ben Carter
Principal Account Exec | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cloudworks_private_offer_term_sheet.pdf (stub)]
[Attachment: sku_channel_margin_breakout.xlsx (stub)]

Subject: Re: Draft: CloudWorks private-offer term sheet + channel margin breakout

Thanks everyone — that draft is exactly the level of detail Procurement needed. Quick alignment and next steps: 

- CloudWorks indicated preference for Model A (pass-through credit) in our call — it preserves your reconciliation flow and keeps reseller commissioning separate. Ben / Irene: can you confirm the marketplace listing steps for Model A (we need to ensure the reseller accounts are linked for credit delivery)?

- Andrew: please confirm the provisional SKU mix in the CSV and return any changes by EOD Monday 6/14 so we can finalize numbers for the legal term sheet.

- Irene: please prepare the invoice-level mock and an ops checklist (marketplace entitlements, reseller account mapping, and billing codes) so CloudWorks can loop Procurement. Ideally share that checklist as an internal Drive doc we can make visible to their team.

I'll coordinate scheduling for Legal/Procurement handshake once we have the finalized numbers. Thanks — feel free to accept the DocuSign preview Ben included if Procurement prefers that route.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
